infrastructure: Digicel PNG providing basic mobile connectivity; Coral Sea Cable System improving international bandwidth
PNG DataCo national network company; urban centres (Port Moresby, Lae) have improving connectivity
Vast geography (460,000 km²) with 800+ languages creates major infrastructure deployment challenges
talent: University of PNG and PNG University of Technology producing very limited CS cohorts
Very small urban educated workforce; most population subsistence agricultural
Brain drain to Australia significant among educated Papua New Guineans
governance: ICT Act and developing data protection framework

DICT released a Draft National Sovereign Digital Transformation and AI Strategy for public consultation (Mar 2026), following a draft AI Adoption Framework (Feb 2026) — both still drafts, not yet formally adopted
Governance constrained by significant corruption and weak institutional capacity
investment: Resource sector (ExxonMobil LNG, Barrick Gold) driving some industrial IoT investment
Very limited domestic tech investment; mostly development aid-funded digital projects
PNG Sustainable Development Program providing limited tech co-investment
economic_readiness: 9.5M population; resource-dependent economy with very limited digital market formation
Mobile money (MiBank, BSP) growing as primary digital financial access point
Extreme geographic and linguistic fragmentation creating unique challenges for any AI deployment
